name: cua
description: Scale computer-use 2.0 with open-source drivers, cross-OS fleets, and benchmarks for training, evaluation, and data generation.
one_liner: Gives an AI agent a virtual computer it can click around on, type into, and take screenshots of, just like a human employee would use software that has no API.
buyer: An operations manager at an insurance or logistics company who is stuck with an old desktop application that has no API and no plans to ever get one.
business_use_cases: Automate data entry into a 20-year-old legacy insurance claims application that only has a Windows GUI.
Run overnight QA test suites that click through a web or desktop app exactly like a real tester would, catching visual regressions.
Offer 'RPA replacement' service to back-office teams still paying for expensive robotic process automation licenses.

money_ideas.idea: Sell managed automation setups for specific legacy apps (insurance, healthcare back-office) as a service.
Charge per cloud-desktop-hour for companies that don't want to run their own fleet infrastructure.
Consulting engagements to script one-off automations for a client's specific painful manual workflow.

steal_this: Pick one boring, repetitive desktop task (e.g. copying data from an old ERP screen into a spreadsheet) and sell it as a done-for-you automation to a single local business this weekend.
